name: PT2399 echo
subtitle: Archetype · digital delay chip in an analog-feeling circuit · resistor-set clock

keyIdea.eli5: One resistor on pin 6 sets the chip's clock, like the speed of a conveyor belt of tiny buckets. Slower belt, longer echo, but fewer buckets per second, so long echoes sound darker and grittier.
keyIdea.detail: Feedback sends some of the echo back onto the belt for more repeats.

summary: The dry signal goes straight to the output. A copy goes through filter → chip memory → filter, and part of that is fed back in.

top.label: +5 V regulated (from 9 V)
top.eli5: Red is a calm 5 V made from the 9 V battery by a regulator, because the chip would fry on 9 V.

bottom.label: 0 V (ground)
bottom.eli5: Blue is the battery's − side and ground.

notes: There's no PT2399 model in Falstad, so this is behavioral only. Design equations: https://electricdruid.net/useful-design-equations-for-the-pt2399/

job.eli5: Splits the guitar into a dry road and a road into the chip.

wire.eli5: The guitar, split two ways: dry and into the chip.

job.eli5: Filter in, record into memory, play back later, filter out.
Sends some echo back in for more repeats, and blends the echoes with the dry note.
A pressure reducer: it turns the battery's 9 V into a calm 5 V.

order.eli5: Between the battery and the chip.

breaks.eli5: The chip gets 9 V and dies, or gets nothing: no echo.

job.eli5: A polite listener that copies the guitar for both roads.

breaks.eli5: The two roads pull on each other and the pickup.

chip.note: The source uses a dual op-amp here; a TL072 is a typical choice.

job.eli5: A sieve that removes very high sounds before recording, so they don't come back as metallic junk.

breaks.eli5: Metallic, whistly echoes (aliasing: high sounds folding down into wrong notes).

tune.higher: Bigger anti-alias cap: darker echoes, less fizz from the digital part.
tune.lower: Smaller: brighter, with more digital grit.
tune.tooFar: Too small and the clock's whine sneaks in.

job.eli5: A tiny tape recorder: it turns sound into numbers, stores them, and plays them back a moment later.
job.detail: ADC means analog-to-digital converter; DAC is the reverse.

use.6: The Time pot plus its minimum resistor go from here to ground.

job.eli5: The echo-time knob: more resistance slows the clock and stretches the echo.
job.detail: A fixed resistor in series keeps the knob from going too low and locking the chip.

tune.higher: Bigger time resistance: the chip's clock slows, so the echo waits longer and gets darker and grittier.
tune.lower: Smaller: the clock speeds up, so the echo comes back sooner and cleaner.
tune.tooFar: The datasheet table runs from 0.5 Ω (31 ms) to 27.6k (342 ms) and warns against under 1k at power-on. Past the table the clock gets so slow the echo turns to crunchy, aliased lo-fi.

job.eli5: A second sieve that smooths the chip's tiny steps and hides its clock whine.

order.eli5: Right after the chip plays back.

breaks.eli5: A high whine and grainy steps.

tune.higher: Bigger reconstruction cap: smoother, darker repeats.
tune.lower: Smaller: brighter repeats with more hiss.
tune.tooFar: Too small and you hear the chip's clock as a whine.

job.eli5: The repeats knob: how much echo goes back onto the belt.
job.detail: Past a point it feeds itself and runs away into oscillation.

order.eli5: From the echo output back to the chip's input.

tune.tooFar: Far off and runaway oscillation sits at one end.
tune.real: This sketch does not model it.

job.eli5: How loud the echoes are next to the dry note.

order.eli5: Between the echo and the mixer.

tune.lower: Smaller: it loads the mixer a little.
tune.tooFar: Very small and it drags the level down.
tune.real: This sketch does not model it.

job.eli5: A mixing bowl that adds dry and echo without them pushing on each other.

breaks.eli5: The two roads interfere; the mix gets unpredictable.

chip.note: The second half of the dual op-amp mixes the echo with the dry sound.

groundNote.eli5: Ground here is the battery's − side (negative ground), the usual setup.

honestyNote.eli5: The echo timing and darkening are right in spirit. Noise, grit and the chip's exact filters aren't simulated. The board view is an auto-generated perfboard sketch.

honesty.eli5: Approximated with a Web Audio delay line and a filter that darkens long delays. The real chip adds grit and noise that the model leaves out.
Modeled as real feedback in the delay line.
